absent: System call numbers, entry points and error returns that consume these flags, commands and records.
Locking rules, ordering constraints and concurrency guarantees for advisory, open file description and flock style locks.
Runtime state machines and side effects for terminal controls, packet mode, memory mappings, sync and advice operations.
Kernel internal dispatch, validation and privilege checks for ioctl codes, hugetlb selections and poll notifications.
Architecture specific values for optional flock padding, extra system identification and mode width dependent layouts beyond the generic forms shown.

findings.text: Open behavior flags use single bit positions with O_NONBLOCK at 11, O_DSYNC at 12, FASYNC at 13, O_DIRECT at 14, O_LARGEFILE at 15, O_DIRECTORY at 16, O_NOFOLLOW at 17, O_NOATIME at 18, O_CLOEXEC at 19, internal __O_SYNC at 20 combined with O_DSYNC to form O_SYNC, O_PATH at 21, internal __O_TMPFILE at 22 combined with O_DIRECTORY to form O_TMPFILE, and O_EMPTYPATH at 26, while O_NDELAY aliases O_NONBLOCK.

File control operation codes map as F_DUPFD 0, F_GETFD 1, F_SETFD 2, F_GETFL 3, F_SETFL 4, F_GETLK 5, F_SETLK 6, F_SETLKW 7, F_SETOWN 8, F_GETOWN 9, F_SETSIG 10, F_GETSIG 11, F_GETLK64 12, F_SETLK64 13, F_SETLKW64 14 tied to 64 bit lock records, F_SETOWN_EX 15, F_GETOWN_EX 16, F_GETOWNER_UIDS 17, F_OFD_GETLK 36, F_OFD_SETLK 37, F_OFD_SETLKW 38, with owner selectors F_OWNER_TID 0, F_OWNER_PID 1 and F_OWNER_PGRP 2.
Descriptor and lock kind values map as FD_CLOEXEC 1 where any low bit set counts, F_RDLCK 0, F_WRLCK 1, F_UNLCK 2, F_EXLCK 4 and F_SHLCK 8.

Flock style locking distinguishes LOCK_SH 1 for shared hold, LOCK_EX 2 for exclusive hold, LOCK_NB 4 as modifier combined with a hold to avoid waiting, LOCK_UN 8 to release, LOCK_MAND 32 for mandatory mode, LOCK_READ 64 allowing concurrent reads, LOCK_WRITE 128 allowing concurrent writes and LOCK_RW 192 allowing both, with F_LINUX_SPECIFIC_BASE 1024 reserving vendor codes upward.

Ownership exception record f_owner_ex holds field type of integer kind selecting thread versus process versus group interpretation followed by field pid of kernel process identifier kind naming the target.

Lock description records flock and flock64 each list field l_type of short kind for lock kind, field l_whence of short kind for reference point, fields l_start and l_len for offset range, and field l_pid of kernel process identifier kind for owner, with classic flock using native offset width and flock64 using 64 bit offset width, each permitting optional trailing architecture supplied identification or padding fields.

Huge page size selection uses HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_SHIFT 26 and HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_MASK hex 3F, with size codes HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_16KB at shift 14, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_64KB at 16, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_512KB at 19, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_1MB at 20, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_2MB at 21, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_8MB at 23, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_16MB at 24, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_32MB at 25, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_256MB at 28, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_512MB at 29, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_1GB at 30, HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_2GB at 31 and HUGETLB_FLAG_ENCODE_16GB at 34, each placed at the shared shift.

Fixed width model maps __s8 to signed char, __u8 to unsigned char, __s16 to signed short, __u16 to unsigned short, __s32 to signed int, __u32 to unsigned int, and __s64 plus __u64 to signed and unsigned long long, with two spellings for the 64 bit pair differing only by extension keyword for strict modes.

Control code fields use widths _IOC_NRBITS 8, _IOC_TYPEBITS 8, _IOC_SIZEBITS 14 and _IOC_DIRBITS 2, laid from low bits upward as number, type, size then direction, with masks _IOC_NRMASK, _IOC_TYPEMASK, _IOC_SIZEMASK and _IOC_DIRMASK holding all ones of each width and shifts _IOC_NRSHIFT at 0, _IOC_TYPESHIFT after number, _IOC_SIZESHIFT after type and _IOC_DIRSHIFT after size.

Direction values use _IOC_NONE 0, _IOC_WRITE 1 and _IOC_READ 2 with combined read write for bidirectional transfer, code builder _IOC places direction type number and size into their slots, size helper _IOC_TYPECHECK derives from referenced type size, checked builders _IO, _IOR, _IOW and _IOWR supply none read write or combined direction with derived size while _IOR_BAD, _IOW_BAD and _IOWR_BAD use explicit size, decoders _IOC_DIR, _IOC_NR and _IOC_SIZE recover direction number and size by shift and mask, and helpers IOC_IN, IOC_OUT, IOC_INOUT, IOCSIZE_MASK and IOCSIZE_SHIFT expose shifted direction bits plus size mask and shift.

Classic line controls use hexadecimal codes TCGETS 5401, TCSETS 5402, TCSETSW 5403, TCSETSF 5404, TCGETA 5405, TCSETA 5406, TCSETAW 5407, TCSETAF 5408, TCSBRK 5409, TCXONC 540A, TCFLSH 540B, TIOCEXCL 540C, TIOCNXCL 540D, TIOCSCTTY 540E, TIOCGPGRP 540F, TIOCSPGRP 5410, TIOCOUTQ 5411, TIOCSTI 5412, TIOCGWINSZ 5413, TIOCSWINSZ 5414, TIOCMGET 5415, TIOCMBIS 5416, TIOCMBIC 5417, TIOCMSET 5418, TIOCGSOFTCAR 5419, TIOCSSOFTCAR 541A, FIONREAD 541B with TIOCINQ as alias, TIOCLINUX 541C, TIOCCONS 541D, TIOCGSERIAL 541E, TIOCSSERIAL 541F, TIOCPKT 5420, FIONBIO 5421, TIOCNOTTY 5422, TIOCSETD 5423, TIOCGETD 5424, TCSBRKP 5425, TIOCSBRK 5427, TIOCCBRK 5428 and TIOCGSID 5429.

Extended controls mix fixed hexadecimal codes and type T encodings as TCGETS2 read 2A, TCSETS2 write 2B, TCSETSW2 write 2C and TCSETSF2 write 2D each with second termios payload, TIOCGRS485 542E, TIOCSRS485 542F, TIOCGPTN read 30 unsigned int, TIOCSPTLCK write 31 int, TIOCGDEV read 32 unsigned int, TCGETX 5432, TCSETX 5433, TCSETXF 5434, TCSETXW 5435, TIOCSIG write 36 int, TIOCVHANGUP 5437, TIOCGPKT read 38 int, TIOCGPTLCK read 39 int, TIOCGEXCL read 40 int, TIOCGPTPEER plain 41, TIOCGISO7816 read 42 and TIOCSISO7816 combined 43 with serial ISO payloads, FIONCLEX 5450, FIOCLEX 5451, FIOASYNC 5452, TIOCSERCONFIG 5453, TIOCSERGWILD 5454, TIOCSERSWILD 5455, TIOCGLCKTRMIOS 5456, TIOCSLCKTRMIOS 5457, TIOCSERGSTRUCT 5458, TIOCSERGETLSR 5459, TIOCSERGETMULTI 545A, TIOCSERSETMULTI 545B, TIOCMIWAIT 545C, TIOCGICOUNT 545D and FIOQSIZE 5460.

Packet mode event bits map as TIOCPKT_DATA 0, TIOCPKT_FLUSHREAD 1, TIOCPKT_FLUSHWRITE 2, TIOCPKT_STOP 4, TIOCPKT_START 8, TIOCPKT_NOSTOP 16, TIOCPKT_DOSTOP 32 and TIOCPKT_IOCTL 64, with serial empty marker TIOCSER_TEMT hex 01.

Permission record ipc64_perm lists field key of key kind, fields uid gid cuid and cgid of 32 bit user and group kinds, field mode of mode kind, field __pad1 of four bytes minus mode width for alignment, field seq of short kind plus field __pad2, and reserved fields __unused1 and __unused2 of unsigned long kind.

Memory protections and mappings map as PROT_READ hex 1, PROT_WRITE hex 2, PROT_EXEC hex 4, PROT_SEM hex 8, PROT_NONE 0, PROT_GROWSDOWN hex 01000000, PROT_GROWSUP hex 02000000, MAP_TYPE hex 0F, MAP_FIXED hex 10, MAP_ANONYMOUS hex 20, MAP_POPULATE hex 008000, MAP_NONBLOCK hex 010000, MAP_STACK hex 020000, MAP_HUGETLB hex 040000, MAP_SYNC hex 080000, MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE hex 100000, MAP_UNINITIALIZED hex 4000000, MAP_FILE 0, MAP_GROWSDOWN hex 0100, MAP_DENYWRITE hex 0800, MAP_EXECUTABLE hex 1000, MAP_LOCKED hex 2000, MAP_NORESERVE hex 4000, PKEY_UNRESTRICTED 0, PKEY_DISABLE_ACCESS 1, PKEY_DISABLE_WRITE 2 with PKEY_ACCESS_MASK combining both, MCL_CURRENT 1, MCL_FUTURE 2, MCL_ONFAULT 4, SHADOW_STACK_SET_TOKEN bit 0 and SHADOW_STACK_SET_MARKER bit 1 of a 64 bit word.

Range sync and advice map as MLOCK_ONFAULT hex 01, MS_ASYNC 1, MS_INVALIDATE 2, MS_SYNC 4, MADV_NORMAL 0, MADV_RANDOM 1, MADV_SEQUENTIAL 2, MADV_WILLNEED 3, MADV_DONTNEED 4, MADV_FREE 8, MADV_REMOVE 9, MADV_DONTFORK 10, MADV_DOFORK 11, MADV_MERGEABLE 12, MADV_UNMERGEABLE 13, MADV_HUGEPAGE 14, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE 15, MADV_DONTDUMP 16, MADV_DODUMP 17, MADV_WIPEONFORK 18, MADV_KEEPONFORK 19, MADV_COLD 20, MADV_PAGEOUT 21, MADV_POPULATE_READ 22, MADV_POPULATE_WRITE 23, MADV_DONTNEED_LOCKED 24, MADV_COLLAPSE 25, MADV_HWPOISON 100, MADV_SOFT_OFFLINE 101, MADV_GUARD_INSTALL 102 and MADV_GUARD_REMOVE 103.

Queue descriptor msqid64_ds starts with field msg_perm of permission record kind, then timestamp fields msg_stime msg_rtime and msg_ctime stored as one long each on 64 bit builds and as split low plus high unsigned words on 32 bit builds, followed by counts msg_cbytes msg_qnum and msg_qbytes of unsigned long kind, identifiers msg_lspid and msg_lrpid of process identifier kind, and reserved __unused4 and __unused5.
Platform parameters map as __USER_HZ 100, HZ aliasing user rate, EXEC_PAGESIZE 4096, NOGROUP negative 1 and MAXHOSTNAMELEN 64.

Poll masks use hexadecimal bits POLLIN 0001, POLLPRI 0002, POLLOUT 0004, POLLERR 0008, POLLHUP 0010, POLLNVAL 0020, POLLRDNORM 0040, POLLRDBAND 0080, POLLWRNORM 0100, POLLWRBAND 0200, POLLMSG 0400, POLLREMOVE 1000, POLLRDHUP 2000, POLLFREE 4000 and POLL_BUSY_LOOP 8000 with the last two carrying poll type qualification.
Poll record pollfd holds field fd of integer kind for descriptor followed by field events of short kind for requested mask and field revents of short kind for returned mask.

Kernel scalar aliases map __kernel_long_t to long, __kernel_ulong_t to unsigned long, __kernel_ino_t to unsigned long, __kernel_mode_t to unsigned int, __kernel_pid_t and __kernel_ipc_pid_t to int, __kernel_uid_t and __kernel_gid_t to unsigned int, __kernel_suseconds_t to long, __kernel_daddr_t to int, __kernel_uid32_t and __kernel_gid32_t to unsigned int, and __kernel_old_uid_t plus __kernel_old_gid_t to the current user and group aliases.
Each generic user header defines a single inclusion guard macro marking the header as included to prevent repeated processing.

Several user layouts vary by configuration and need matched handling across builds as lock records may gain trailing architecture fields, permission padding depends on mode width, and queue timestamps switch between single word and split word forms by word size.
